evidence_paraphrase: env_ac_rme provides model-based RME estimates; individual-country estimates are either reported by national statistical institutes or estimated by Eurostat.
For countries that do not report, Eurostat includes country estimates produced with the Python country RME tool.
supports: Python country RME tool and non-reporter treatment

evidence_paraphrase: Country MFA-RME reporting is voluntary; Eurostat also performs country-level model estimations.
Country env_ac_rme data are updated in July for country-reported data and in November for Eurostat estimates.
RMC estimates are not directly observable; assumptions and modelling techniques determine results, and Eurostat country estimates use the Python tool.

Eurostat-produced estimates and country data using Eurostat’s tool have harmonized methodologies, while country-specific models can hamper cross-country comparability; average EU RME coefficients may be suboptimal especially for smaller economies.
Country-level comparison over time is considered good and explicitly better than cross-country comparability.
The dataset includes country-reported estimates for about half of Member States; Eurostat country estimates are benchmarked to the EU model.
supports: mixed provenance in disseminated country data

evidence_paraphrase: Eurostat country estimates use the Python tool, while countries may use Eurostat’s country RME tool or a country-specific model.
supports: Eurostat tool versus own national models

evidence_paraphrase: Eurostat publishes a country RME tool, handbook and input-data file to facilitate country-level RME compilation.
The published country-tool package is a combined handbook, Excel-based tool and auxiliary data pool.
The country tool was designed to comply with EU-model concepts/methods/data and to provide a harmonized approach for Member States.
The Python tool follows the handbook but differs from the Excel route through FIGARO-based trade inputs, whole-EU calibration and several additional adjustments.
supports: Python and public Excel tool are not byte-for-byte/method-identical routes

evidence_paraphrase: The public data pool contains most inputs, but model-specific Comext data in the RME182 classification and its conversion procedure are available on request from Eurostat.
Code i means value imputed by Eurostat or other receiving agencies; it is a generic observation-status code.
The former s code (Eurostat estimate) was changed to i, whose current definition is broader than Eurostat-only estimation.
supports: why i alone cannot identify an RMC production method

evidence_paraphrase: The GHG-footprint model applies the same method to all countries, although some non-European input emissions are themselves estimated by Eurostat and are less accurate.
supports: GHG cross-country procedural consistency and residual model limitations

evidence_paraphrase: The same method and data sources are applied to all reference years and the complete footprint time series is re-estimated each year.
supports: GHG time-series comparability and revision practice

evidence_paraphrase: GHG footprints are estimated with Leontief-type modelling using air-emissions accounts/Eurostat estimates and FIGARO inter-country input-output tables.
FIGARO provides a consistent annual series from 2010 and has historically revised the full available time series with new releases.
